description: We are a diverse, passionate, and collaborative group of 6 members combining expertise in software development, biomedical engineering, data analytics, and space tech innovation. Together, we are bridging the gap between cutting-edge technology and human spaceflight safety.
summary:
ASTROHEALTH is an astronaut health-monitoring application developed by Team ASTROGUARD to address the challenge of monitoring astronauts' health during space missions. We built a web-based prototype that brings key health information into a centralized dashboard, including heart rate, sleep duration, physical activity, and wellness check-ins. The system uses a React frontend, a FastAPI backend, and a PostgreSQL database to organize health observations, astronaut profiles, and alerts.

ASTRAHEALTH aims to help astronauts and mission support teams understand health trends, identify potentially concerning changes, and make more informed decisions. Its structured design also allows future expansion with additional physiological measurements, wearable-device data, and AI-assisted health insights.

This project is important because astronauts operate in demanding environments where continuous attention to physical and mental well-being is essential. By making health information easier to monitor and interpret, ASTRAHEALTH supports safer, more informed human space exploration.

Demonstration readings are simulated or manually entered, not live astronaut telemetry.
details:
ASTOAHEALTH – Project Details

1. What Does ASTOAHEALTH Do?

ASTOAHEALTH is a web-based astronaut health-monitoring application developed by Team ASTROGUARD to support astronaut well-being during space missions. It provides a centralized platform for organizing and viewing important health observations, helping astronauts and mission support teams better understand changes in health indicators.

The current prototype focuses on a single astronaut and includes health measurements and observations such as heart rate, sleep duration, physical activity, and wellness check-ins. Its structured design also supports additional physiological metrics, including oxygen saturation (SpO₂) and body temperature, as the application evolves.

2. How Does It Work?

The application follows a frontend-backend-database architecture. Users interact with the frontend dashboard, which communicates with the backend through APIs. The backend processes requests, manages health records, and retrieves relevant information from the database.

Health observations are organized with their timestamps, metric types, values, units, and data origins. This helps distinguish simulated or manually entered observations from potential future device-based data. The system also includes structured records for astronaut profiles and health alerts.

3. Benefits and Intended Impact

ASTROHEALTH aims to make astronaut health information easier to access, organize, and interpret. Its intended benefits include:

  • Providing a centralized view of important health observations.
  • Supporting the identification of potentially concerning changes in health measurements.
  • Helping users understand health trends over time.
  • Organizing health information for better-informed decisions.
  • Providing a foundation for future integration with wearable sensors and research datasets.

Ultimately, our goal is to contribute to safer and more informed human space exploration by making astronaut health information more accessible and structured.

4. Technologies and Tools Used

We developed the prototype using the following technologies:

  • Frontend: React, Vite, JavaScript, HTML, CSS and Tailwind CSS.
  • Backend: Python and FastAPI.
  • Database: PostgreSQL and Supabase.
  • Data Validation: Pydantic.
  • Database Management: SQLAlchemy.
  • Version Control: Git and GitHub.
  • Development Environment: Visual Studio Code.

The architecture is designed to support future AI-assisted health insights and additional integrations.

5. Creativity and Innovation

The creative aspect of ASTROHEALTH is its focus on bringing multiple astronaut health observations into one structured monitoring platform. Rather than treating every measurement as an isolated value, the system organizes observations by metric, time, unit, and data origin. This provides a foundation for understanding health patterns and developing more advanced decision-support capabilities.

We also considered the importance of distinguishing actual research information from demonstration data, ensuring that simulated readings are not misrepresented as real astronaut telemetry.

6. Factors Considered During Development

Our team considered the demanding conditions of space missions, the importance of astronaut physical and mental well-being, data organization, usability, scalability, and the reliability of health information.

We explored NASA's Open Science Data Repository (OSDR), including the Inspiration4 study OSD-575, as a research reference to understand spaceflight-related biological and physiological research. This research helped inform our understanding of astronaut health monitoring. The study was explored as a reference and has not been integrated as live telemetry into our application's health records.

7. Future Vision

ASTROHEALTH is designed as an extensible foundation. Future development could include wearable-device integration, real-time health data collection, additional physiological indicators, historical trend analysis, AI-assisted recommendations, and more advanced alert mechanisms.

Our long-term vision is to evolve ASTROHEALTH into a comprehensive astronaut health-support platform that helps astronauts and mission teams make better-informed decisions throughout space missions.
